newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurds in fierce fighting for strategic dam.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds in fierce fighting for strategic dam.

text.p: Rival Kurdish forces were engaged in fierce fighting on Sunday for control of northern Iraq's strategic Dukan Dam ahead of U.S. peace talks to end the fighting.
Witnesses said Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) forces stalled an advance by their Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) rivals who had pushed to within five km (three miles) of the dam.

A KDP Toyota landcruiser with a machinegun mounted on it lay burned and mangled by the side of a road near the frontline, hit by what the group said was a PUK rocket-propelled grenade in close combat.
The charred bodies of KDP fighters were inside the vehicle. The corpses of five other people were strewn on the roadside nearby, apparently victims of another PUK attack.
The KDP fired 155-mm shells towards PUK forces defending the dam. The PUK returned lighter artillery fire.

Massoud Barzani's KDP, which received Iraqi military backing during earlier fighting in August, were attempting to take the dam in a push to recapture their rival's stronghold Sulaimaniya, the mountainous region's biggest city.
